title: Move More, Sit Less
hook: Even if you hit the gym, hours of unbroken sitting carry their own health risk. Breaking up the day with movement matters as much as the workout.
key_points: Long, unbroken sitting is a health risk in its own right.
Breaking up sitting with short bursts of movement helps — stand, walk, stretch.
Everyday activity counts: stairs, walking, chores all add up.
Some activity is always better than none, at any fitness level.
content_html: Here's the catch even regular exercisers miss: you can do your morning workout and still spend the next nine hours sitting nearly motionless — and that long, unbroken sitting carries its own risk. The fix isn't just more gym time; it's weaving movement through the whole day.
extra_html: The World Health Organization makes two complementary points. First, prolonged sitting is associated with poorer health outcomes, so it's worth breaking up — stand, stretch, or take a short walk every so often rather than staying glued to a chair for hours. Second, everyday movement counts: taking the stairs, walking to the shops, and doing chores all add to your activity total, not just formal exercise. And the most encouraging part of WHO's message is that some activity is always better than none, at any age or starting point. You don't have to be an athlete — you just have to move more and sit less.

related.title: How Much Exercise You Actually Need
related.hook: The headline number is smaller than most people fear: about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — roughly 20-some minutes a day — moves the needle on your health.

related.title: Why Strength Training Matters
related.hook: Cardio gets the glory, but lifting, resistance bands, and bodyweight moves protect something running can't: the muscle and bone you'll rely on for decades.

related.title: Staying Strong as You Age
related.hook: The decline we associate with old age is partly the result of doing less. Staying active — in four distinct ways — keeps you independent far longer.

flashcards.prompt: Why does 'sit less' matter even if you exercise regularly?
flashcards.back_html: Long stretches of unbroken sitting carry their own health risk, separate from how much you work out. Breaking up sitting with short bursts of movement — standing, walking, stretching — helps regardless of your fitness level.

flashcards.prompt: What does WHO say about doing a small amount of activity?

choices.text: Some activity is always better than none
Activity only counts if it's a structured gym workout
Light everyday movement provides no benefit at all

flashcards.explanation_html: WHO stresses that some physical activity is better than none, and that everyday movement — walking, stairs, chores — all counts toward your total.
